title: Natural Domain and Range of a Shifted Square Root Function
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Natural Domain and Range
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and range of the real-valued function defined by f(x) = 1 - sqrt(x).

steps.title: Formulate Radicand Non-Negativity Condition
steps.explanation: The formula involves the principal square root sqrt(x). In the real number system, the square root of a negative number is undefined, so x must be non-negative.
steps.why: Even-indexed roots are defined in the real number system only when the radicand is non-negative.

steps.title: State the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: There are no other operations restricting the input, so the natural domain consists of all non-negative real numbers, [0, inf).
steps.why: The principal square root is the sole algebraic restriction governing the formula.

steps.title: Bound the Output Expression
steps.explanation: The principal square root sqrt(x) takes all values in [0, inf). Multiplying by -1 reverses the inequality to give -sqrt(x) <= 0, and adding 1 shifts the upper bound to 1.
steps.why: Multiplying an inequality by a negative number reverses the direction of the inequality.

steps.title: State the Range in Interval Notation
steps.explanation: At x = 0, f(0) = 1 - 0 = 1. As x increases without bound, sqrt(x) grows without bound, so 1 - sqrt(x) decreases toward negative infinity, covering (-inf, 1].
steps.why: The square root function is continuous, strictly increasing, and unbounded above on [0, inf).
